problem: High cloud infrastructure costs on Kubernetes clusters due to overprovisioned CPU/RAM buffers and complex manual autoscaling configurations.
target_customer: DevOps engineers and Engineering Leaders managing AWS/GCP Kubernetes workloads with over $20k/mo cloud spend.
solution: Autonomous AI agent that dynamically analyzes real-time workload telemetry and automatically right-sizes pod allocations and node groups without downtime.
pain_points: Engineers spend 10+ hours per week manually tuning HPA and resource requests
Cloud bills regularly exceed forecasts by 30-40%
Over-provisioning is the default fear response to avoid SLA outages
assumptions: DevOps teams will grant autonomous write permissions to an AI agent for cluster pod spec edits
Cloud providers will not release a native zero-touch cost optimizer that makes third parties obsolete
risks: Misconfiguration could trigger cascading pod evictions causing downtime
Enterprise infosec friction regarding read/write cluster access
missing_information: Current pilot traction and customer interview counts
Exact pricing unit metric (per node vs % of savings)

first_question.text: What level of access or proof of safety do your enterprise pilot prospects require before letting an agent mutate cluster state?
